basicMistakes.where: After Select winner, the card is unchanged from the plain on-air state. Neither corner is marked as the winner.
After Lock it in, the card is unchanged. No winner or locked decision appears anywhere.
After Select winner then Lock, the only change is that the centre yellow divider becomes a solid line. No boxer is shown as the winner, so the decision the brief needs never appears in any frame.
Grey discs under the RED CORNER / BLUE CORNER tags are empty placeholders. With the brief's own values, no gym logo shows and no gym name appears.

otherProblems: Gym logos sit on their own flat grey disc plates (G-4, G-63, G-64). The white shield on light grey looks washed out, and the disc reads as a placeholder rather than designed furniture.
In the sample frames the grey discs hold nothing, so they look like broken image slots.
With long values the blue corner's name drops to a much smaller size than the red corner's (G-4, G-10). The two sides look unequal.
The lower part of each panel is empty below the record line, and the blue side has even more dead space, so the panels look bottom-heavy and unbalanced.
Select and Clear give no visible feedback, so an operator cannot tell the state of the decision from the program output.
answer.reasons: The basic layout is clean and readable: red and blue panels, a clear weight-class line, and long Irish and Lithuanian names that wrap without clipping. But the card fails the brief's main job after the bout. Select winner and Lock it in never show a winner. Locking only makes the yellow divider solid, so the decision never reaches air. With the brief's own values, the logo slots are empty grey discs and no gym is named. When logos do appear, they sit on grey plates. Long names also shrink one side's type relative to the other. It does not air as delivered.

otherProblems: The suspense step barely changes the board: names dim a little and the panel grows slightly (G-17 to G-22), so viewers will hardly see a suspense beat.
When the long category sets in a smaller size (G-5, G-38), the gap between the title and the gold rule gets a little wider than in the sample state. Viewers are unlikely to notice.
answer.reasons: This is a centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame. The text is clean and centred, and the type hierarchy is clear. The near-opaque panel keeps everything readable over the video, light and busy grounds, which matters for the bright LED wall. The long names, film titles and the long category all fit inside the frame without clipping (G-5 to G-7, G-44, G-45). The reveal outlines the winner in gold and greys out the other nominees, and that reads well. The take, the out and the category update all animate cleanly. Both suspense and reveal are on the operator surface. The only weakness is how faint the suspense state is, and that does not stop it going on air.

otherProblems: When there is no avatar, the fallback monogram shows 'N' next to 'Jürgen_Größenwahn_Müller'. The initial doesn't match the donor's name, which looks slightly off.
With empty values the panel is all dark except the 'DONATION' label, leaving a large blank area. This is an edge case the live alerts should never hit.
The thin orange timer line at the bottom right of the panel is very faint. It is a small detail rather than a fault.
answer.reasons: This is a clean dark alert card at the top right: an orange accent bar, a round avatar, an orange mono label with the amount, a bold white name and a grey message. It stays readable over the video, light and busy backgrounds. The long umlaut name fits on one line. The long message wraps to two lines and ends in a clean ellipsis. The white shield avatar reads well inside its ringed circle on the dark panel. Take, Out and Update all animate cleanly. The operator surface offers all four actions the brief needs, and each one works in the frames: Hold keeps the alert up past 10 s, Resume lets it time out, Replay brings it back in again, and Skip clears it. Nothing overlaps, clips or loses contrast. The only flaws are small: the 'N' fallback initial and the empty-values state.

basicMistakes.where: After Select winner, neither corner panel changes at all: no highlight, no WINNER tag, no dimming of the loser. The decision is never shown on the card.
Lock it in after Select winner only turns the centre divider into a solid yellow line. It still doesn't show who won, so the brief's winner call never reaches air.
Grey logo discs under RED CORNER and BLUE CORNER are empty on the brief's own sample values. Two blank placeholder circles sit in the middle of each panel.

missingActions: select (the button exists, but pressing it shows no winner)
lock (only restyles the divider line; still no winner shown)
otherProblems: When the gym logos do appear (G-4, G-63, G-64), each sits on its own grey disc plate. The disc is too dull for the white crest and gives the dark crest little contrast.
The dark-green-and-black gym logo renders as navy, not in its real colours.
The two sides are unbalanced in the long-value frames: the red name is set much larger than the blue name, which is shrunk to two smaller lines (G-4, G-10).
The weight class disappears completely when that value is empty (G-6), leaving a gap above the panels.
On the brief's sample values the blue panel's lower third is empty dead space under the short name.
answer.reasons: I wouldn't put this graphic on air as delivered. The face-off card itself is clean, and the long Irish and Lithuanian names stay inside their panels. But the core job after the bout doesn't work. Select winner changes nothing on screen. Lock only turns the divider into a solid yellow line. Clear has nothing to undo. So the judges' decision never appears on the card. On the brief's own sample values the gym logos are two empty grey discs. When the logos do load, they sit on grey plates that hurt the dark crest's contrast.

basicMistakes.where: After Select winner, the card looks exactly like the plain face-off in G-17. Neither corner shows a winner mark, highlight or label.

After Select winner and then Lock it in, the only change is that the yellow centre divider extends below the panels. No winner appears anywhere on the card, so the decision the brief needs is never shown.
The gym-logo circles above both names are plain grey discs with nothing in them, in every sample-value frame (also G-16, G-22, G-29, G-35).

missingActions: select: choosing a winner produces no visible change (G-18 to G-23)
lock: locking after a selection only stretches the yellow divider and shows no locked winner (G-46 to G-51)
otherProblems: Each gym logo sits on its own grey circular plate (G-4, G-63, G-64). The white crest on light grey has weak contrast, and the dark logo looks navy on grey rather than dark green and black.
With long values, the blue-corner name is set much smaller than the red-corner name (G-4, G-10), so the two sides look unequal.
In the sample frames the gym name is missing and only the record shows, so the record line sits differently on each side.
Clear pick (G-30 to G-35, G-52 to G-57) can't be judged because a pick never showed in the first place.
answer.reasons: G would not air. The face-off card itself is clean and readable: red and blue panels, a VS badge, the weight-class line, and Irish and Lithuanian names that wrap well and keep their accents. But the brief's main job after the bout is to show the winner, and selecting and locking never do. The card stays the same, apart from the yellow divider growing longer on lock. The logo circles are empty grey discs in the sample frames, and when logos do appear they sit on grey plates. Long names also get unequal type sizes on the two sides.

otherProblems: The amount (€25) sits in small grey monospace after the orange label, so it is quieter than it should be for the key number in a donation alert.
In the sample frames the avatar fallback shows 'N', which does not match the donor's initial (Jürgen).
The short orange timer hairline in the bottom-right corner is very faint and could read as a stray mark rather than a countdown.
With empty values the panel shows only 'DONATION' in a large empty box (G-8 to G-10). This is a degenerate state, not a delivered one.
answer.reasons: This would go on air as delivered. It is a clean dark top-right alert with an orange accent bar, a circular avatar, the label and amount, a bold username and a grey message line. It stays readable over the video, light and busy grounds. The long umlaut username fits. The long message wraps to two lines and ends in a clean ellipsis inside the panel. The white shield avatar sits on dark inside an orange ring, so it stays visible. All four operator actions are offered and behave correctly in the frames: hold keeps the alert up at 10 s, resume lets it time out, replay animates it in again, and skip clears it. The Take, Update and Out transitions are clean. The problems left are small design nits (the quiet amount, the 'N' fallback, the faint timer line), and none of them breaks the graphic.

otherProblems: The suspense state is very subtle: the names dim slightly and the board grows a little. On air it barely reads as a change.
With the long category, the title is set smaller, which leaves a looser gap between the title and the gold rule than in the normal layout. Viewers would hardly notice.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board. It has an opaque panel, a double gold frame, a centred heading with a gold rule, and four evenly spaced nominee rows. It reads well over the dark video, the light ground and the busy ground. The long names, film titles and the long category all fit inside the frame without clipping. The reveal step clearly picks out the winner with a gold box and gold name and dims the other nominees, and they stay readable. Both actions the brief needs, suspense and reveal, are available. The take and out animations are tidy. The only weakness is that the suspense state is understated, and that is not a reason to keep it off air.

otherProblems: The Suspense state is very subtle: the names dim slightly and the frame shifts a little, so a viewer may not see a change on cue.
With the long category, the title steps down to a smaller size and leaves a slightly larger gap above the gold rule than the short title does (G-5, G-34 to G-38). It is a minor rhythm change.
The panel is slightly translucent, so the busy ground shows faintly through it (G-4, G-7, G-10). The text stays fully legible.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, centred black-and-gold board with a double gold frame. The hierarchy is clear: kicker, then category, then a centred rule, then four rows of director and film title. The text is large and high-contrast on the light, video and busy grounds. The long stress names and the long category stay well inside the panel, with no clipping or collisions. Reveal clearly shows the winner in a gold-outlined, gold-filled row with even padding and dims the other nominees, who stay readable. Suspense and Reveal are both on the operator surface. The Take and Out transitions are clean, and the empty state shows only the category, centred. The only issues are small: a subtle suspense cue and a slight spacing change with the long title. Neither would keep it off air.

otherProblems: With the sample values the avatar shows an 'N' placeholder initial, which doesn't match the donor name 'Jürgen_Größenwahn_Müller'.

A short, faint orange line sits in the panel's bottom-right corner (about x 1680–1795). It stays the same length whether the alert is held or counting down, so it reads as a leftover rather than a timer bar.
With every field empty, the panel shows only 'DONATION' and a large empty area.
answer.reasons: A clean, well-padded dark panel at top right with an orange accent bar. The label, amount, name and message are readable over the video, light and busy backgrounds. The long name with umlauts fits, and the long message wraps to two lines and ends in a clean ellipsis inside the panel. The white avatar holds up inside its orange ring. All four operator actions work as the brief needs: Hold keeps the alert on at 10 s, Resume lets it time out, Replay re-runs the entrance and Skip clears it at once. The remaining issues (a mismatched placeholder initial, a faint corner line, a sparse empty-values state) are small and don't keep it off air.
